19                On Tuesday, February 3rd, a 

20   Metro-North train departed Grand Central Station 

21   at approximately 5:45, destined for Chappaqua 

22   Train Station.  On board were more than 400 of 

23   my friends, neighbors and constituents returning 

24   to their families after a long hard day of work.  

25   Tragically, five of the passengers and an 


                                                                345

 1   automobile driver never reached their 

 2   destinations.  And less than a week ago, we lost 

 3   some incredible members of our community and 

 4   will continue to mourn their passings:  

 5                Walter Liedtke, curator at the 

 6   Metropolitan Museum of Art for 35 years; 

 7                Robert Dirks, scientist at 

 8   D.E. Shaw Research; 

 9                Joseph Nadol, managing director and 

10   analyst at JPMorgan Chase; 

11                Eric Vandercar, who spent his 

12   career in finance; 

13                Aditya Tomar, a resident of 

14   Danbury, Connecticut, who worked at JPMorgan 

15   Chase; 

16                And Ellen Brody, an active member 

17   of her community who worked at a local jewelry 

18   store.  

19                Six days ago, these people lost 

20   their lives in what was Metro-North's worst 

21   accident in history.  I ask my colleagues to 

22   join me in a moment of silence as we reflect on 

23   the profound tragedy.

 7                THE SECRETARY:   Senator Bonacic, 

 8   from the Committee on Judiciary, reports the 

 9   following nomination:  

10                Judge Leslie E. Stein, to the 

11   New York State Court of Appeals.

12                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

13   Bonacic.

14                SENATOR BONACIC:   Thank you, 

15   Mr. President.

16                Earlier today we had a public 

17   hearing regarding the qualifications of the 

18   nominee, Appellate Division Judge Leslie Stein.  

19                I want to commend the Governor for 

20   sending us a nominee that is very experienced, 

21   19 years through the judicial steps, served as a 

22   Supreme Court judge in Albany for six years, in 

23   the Appellate Division for seven years.  

24                And I met with her personally prior 

25   to today's events.  And pursuant to the 


                                                                349

 1   provisions of Section 2 of Article 6 of the 

 2   Constitution and the provisions of Section 68 of 

 3   the Judiciary Law, the Judiciary Committee has 

 4   reported the nomination to the floor with 

 5   unanimous consent.

 6                Now, Judge Stein is in the house, in 

 7   the gallery, and she's joined by her husband, 

 8   Mark Sonders; their friends Beth Lifshin, who was 

 9   Clark, Regina Martino, the Honorable Karen 

10   Peters, who is the presiding justice of the 

11   Appellate Division of the Third Department, and 

12   Robert Mayberger, the clerk of the Appellate 

13   Division, the Third Department.

14                I now ask you to recognize 

15   Senator Breslin.

17   Breslin.

19   Senator Bonacic.  

20                Thank you, Mr. President.

21                It's my honor to rise and move the 

22   nomination of Leslie Stein, a friend and a fellow 

23   lawyer, a legal practitioner for almost 35 years 

24   in our community, someone who started in college 

25   by reaching Phi Beta Kappa, going to Albany Law, 


                                                                350

 1   graduating second in her class, became a clerk in 

 2   Family Court immediately because she envisioned 

 3   that her future was in public service.  Shortly 

 4   thereafter, moved on, ultimately became a City 

 5   Court judge in the City of Albany.  

 6                Beyond that, she was a member of 

 7   Whalen McNamee Titus & Williams, a very 

 8   prestigious Albany law firm, where she practiced 

 9   for in excess of 13 years at the highest levels, 

10   concentrating on matrimonial law.  

11                Her 19 years in the judiciary, the 

12   last number of which have been in the Appellate 

13   Division, have just furthered exampled her 

14   ability to have an immense background in all 

15   areas of the law beyond the areas she 

16   concentrated in.  

17                She has won approvals from every 

18   possible corner, including the New York State 

19   Bar, who rated her highly qualified, the Trial 

20   Lawyers, who rated her very high qualified.  

21                I know her as someone who is bright, 

22   accessible, professional, and the kind of person 

23   we do want as a judge.  

24                She is a credit to our profession, 

25   she is a credit to our Albany community, and I 


                                                                351

 2   the Court of Appeals.

11   Graffeo, who served with distinction and was a 

12   remarkable judge, and also somebody that I don't 

13   think we've heard the last of.  I'd love to see 

14   her the first woman attorney general, if she 

15   chooses to run.

18   magnificent lawyer and somebody that I know about

20   distinguished law firm, McNamee Titus & Williams 

21   here in Albany.  And he told me, my son Bob told

23   lawyer but a very nice person -- an exceptionally 

24   nice person, ethical and somebody that is 

25   eminently qualified to serve on our highest 


                                                                352

 1   court.

 3   Union College -- one of the finest universities 

 4   in the nation -- right here in Schenectady, and a 

 5   magna cum laude graduate of Albany -- as Senator 

 6   Breslin said, second in her class -- and has been 

 7   an outstanding community citizen.  

 8                You know, one of the qualities of 

 9   any judge is that they have to be a good person.  

10   And this is somebody that not only comes from a 

11   remarkable background -- both her mother and 

12   father were lawyers, her mother a graduate of 

13   Columbia University, one of the first women 

14   practicing law, her late mom and dad.  And I'm

17   accomplish.
